questions.q: Ailments from disappointed love or grief, with weeping alone, aversion to sympathy and a craving for salt, need:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum mur: silent grief.

questions.q: Most of the water filtered by the kidneys is reabsorbed in the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About two-thirds of filtered water.

questions.q: For injury to nerve-rich parts such as crushed fingertips, with shooting pains along the nerve, use:
questions.why: Hypericum is the remedy for nerve injuries.

questions.q: Under current Indian and international guidelines, hypertension in an adult is diagnosed at a clinic BP of at least:
Complaints from loss of vital fluids (haemorrhage, diarrhoea, lactation), with periodicity and great sensitivity to touch, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. China: weakness from loss of fluids.

questions.q: A patient understands speech but cannot speak fluently after a stroke. The lesion is in:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Broca's (areas 44, 45) = motor speech; Wernicke's lesion gives fluent but meaningless speech.

questions.q: The stage of the malaria parasite injected into man by the female Anopheles mosquito is the:
questions.why: Sporozoites from the mosquito's salivary glands enter the blood and go to the liver to begin exo-erythrocytic schizogony.

questions.q: On the ECG, the T wave represents:
opts: conduction delay in the AV node
questions.why: P is atrial depolarisation, QRS ventricular depolarisation and T ventricular repolarisation.

questions.q: Frequent, ineffectual urging for stool in an irritable, sedentary person who lives on stimulants and rich food calls for:
questions.why: Nux vomica: frequent ineffectual urging, passing small quantities, in irritable, zealous, sedentary people; Opium and Alumina have no urging.

questions.q: Fractures that are slow to unite, with pricking pain at the site, are helped by:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Symphytum ('knitbone') promotes union of fractures.
